text:
Nate: quick idea — instead of a periodic full compaction pass, what if we do a tiny "minor-merge" on the eviction path: when an eviction frees a slab, try to merge it with adjacent free slabs of the same size-class. should cut fragmentation growth in long-ctx runs without a stop-the-world job.

Serena: can you post the numbers that motivated this? seeing fragmentation spike in which workload?

Nate: repro is the long-convo-sim (30k token context, mixed chat+info retrieval). heap fragmentation rises ~18% over 2 hours. counters from profiler: 
```
KVArena.free_fragments: 482 -> 1263
KVArena.total_free_bytes: 3.2GB -> 2.1GB
KVArena.allocated_bytes: 11.6GB -> 13.7GB
```

Vikram: hmm that's ugly. is this the TLS allocator or global arena? block-size distribution?

Nate: global arena, size-classes are 4k/8k/16k/32k. majority of frees are 8k-ish but many coalesce opportunities are adjacent physically (due to allocator reuse pattern) but we never stitch unless a compaction pass runs.

Maria: so the cheap approach is opportunistic coalesce: when freeing, check left/right neighbors' header flags and merge if same class. costs one or two pointer updates, no scanning. downside: fragmentation still possible if neighbors allocated. tradeoff seems small.

Vikram: two concerns: 1) need atomicity under concurrent frees (CAS hop)? 2) how does this interact with KV cache paging — if we merge, do we increase contiguous free that makes paging cheaper? probably good. also consider a small threshold: only merge up to N slabs to avoid long free-path stalls.

Nate: I ran a quick microbench: minor-merge enabled (merge up to 2 neighbors) 
- mem footprint drop: ~7% overall at 2h
- p95 latency impact on token gen: +0.3% (noise)
- compaction job frequency needed: went from hourly to maybe once a day in that workload.

infra-bot: CI: compaction-sim/kv-minor-merge (linux-x64) — PASSED. logs: https://ci.internal/reports/compaction-sim/2012345678 (artifact: profiler snapshots) :white_check_mark:

Serena: nice. we should emit metrics so SRE can watch regressions. metrics proposal: `kv.merge.count`, `kv.merge.bytes_reclaimed`, `kv.free_scan_bytes`, and a histogram for merge latency. add a feature flag to roll out.

Vikram: also experiment with block_size tuning in parallel. my hypothesis: larger base block (8k->16k) reduces header churn but increases waste for small objects; merging helps more if base block smaller. quick config to try:
```yaml
kv:
  base_block: 4096 # try 4k vs 8k vs 16k
  max_merge_span: 2
  merge_on_free: true
```

Maria: i'll prototype the merge-on-free in the allocator hot path (safe-lock + fallback to CAS for concurrent frees). i'll add unit tests and a small fuzz harness for concurrency. need a perf harness — @Nate can you drop the long-convo-sim docker image?

Nate: yep i'll upload the sim image + a runbook. plan: prototype this week, run perf regressions + long-run (48h) next week, toggle feature-flag for staging rollout after metrics exist. cc @Serena for SLO implications.

Serena: sounds good. add alert if `kv.merge.count` >> baseline or if p95 increases >1%. :thumbsup:

Nate: thanks — i'll open a PR with draft impl + perf results. will link the CI artifacts in the PR.
